newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slightly weaker in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slightly weaker in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were modestly weaker on Wednesday morning after clawing back some ground from a sharply lower opening, as investors digested the impact of the market's recent sharp gains, brokers said.
"In the long term we could be a good deal higher but we got to this point very quickly, said Julian Ings-Chambers, assistant director of equity sales at BZW Securities.
The Hang Seng Index slipped 28 points to 13,457 in the early morning trade on very heavy volume of HK$5.63 billion. Overnight, the Hang Seng London Reference Index shed only 6.02 point to 13,479.31.
"At 14 times 1997 earnings, the market is looking a little pricey in the short term," said Ing-Chambers.
Using Tuesday's record close, the index has gained about 1,000 points in November and surpassed most 1996 targets, brokers said.
"Most institutional investors seem to be committed to the Hong Kong market, but they have turned cautious at this level, said Janet Gillies, sales executive at OCBC Securities.
"We certainly could go another 500 points, but some long-term investors seem to be ready to sell," she said, adding there was quite a bit of retail investor money in the market now.
Hang Seng Index futures also reversed direction as well. The November contract lost 50 points in early trading and the December contract shed about 40 points.
Amoy Properties led the most active table after the company's placement of 35 million new shares at HK$11.10 each was put through the market.
The share was down HK$0.30 to HK$11.20 in early Wednesday trade after hitting an alltime high of HK$11.90 on Tuesday.
Brokers said the Amoy placement had not been especially well supported in Hong Kong, and investors would see it as capping the share's 1996 rise.
The utility sector was up in early trade. HongKong Telecom, however, was the only utility stock to post a gain, putting on HK$0.15 to HK$13.25. Hongkong Electric lost HK$0.25 to HK$24.65.
Other blue chip sectors were weaker. Property investment stocks came in for some profit-taking following their strong run on the back of the Hysan sale.
Great Eagle shed HK$0.30 to HK$32.30, Henderson Investment lost HK$0.15 to HK$9.45, and Hysan fell HK$0.20 to HK$29.80.
